bullets.title: Can Dying Languages Be Saved?
bullets.creator: Judith Thurman for The New Yorker_
bullets.note: for _The New Yorker_. As longtime readers know, I am obsessed with languages and [language learning](https://tim.blog/category/language/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf). This article checked all the boxes. Fun fact: Another [article from Judith](http://www.newyorker.com/reporting/2008/06/23/080623fa_fact_thurman) prompted the Herzog documentary in the next bullet.

bullets.title: Cave of Forgotten Dreams
bullets.note: ([Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/Cave-Forgotten-Dreams-Werner-Herzog/dp/B0093SOOHU/), [Apple TV](https://itunes.apple.com/us/movie/cave-of-forgotten-dreams/id451797497?cmp=rt_where_to_watch)). Description: “[Werner Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Werner_Herzog)’s award-winning 2011 doc is a thrilling study of 32,000-year-old cave paintings recently discovered in Southern France.” It has [96% on Rotten Tomatoes](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/cave_of_forgotten_dreams), and you can [watch the trailer here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qfJfRx2IAYo).
